goal_checks.notes: ImportCandidate has a page; useImportReview computes the slug, bbox and reading order per candidate's page and queries the session's existing highlights session-wide, ranking each page separately. use-import-review.test.ts proves two pages write in one call to their own pages.

textBoxesFromViewport composes the pdfjs item transform with the viewport transform (the multiplication Util.transform performs) into a display-space box; pdf-text-boxes.test.ts pins the composition and the guards.

useImportSource reads the session's main artifact bytes through the shared/lib/pdf seam, opens the PDF, walks every page and builds rung-1 candidates (annotations + text items); a missing document and an annotation-free document both report why. The control mounts in the rail and renders the review. use-import-source.test.ts and workspace-document.test.tsx pin it.
Fifteen tests across the touched files, and the full suite passes (360 passed / 10 skipped).

matches — rung 1 only; a real /Highlight annotation is exact, so no OCR runs and no page is rasterized.

issues_found: D-02 divergence: this imports the OPEN document's annotations, not a separately uploaded note-slot copy. The upload flow (create the artifact, upload bytes to Storage) is not built and remains a follow-up; recorded in analyze.json and here.
pdfjs v6 removed convertToViewportRectangle; the adapter uses convertToViewportPoint. Worth noting for any other consumer.
The scan walks every page synchronously in the client; a very large PDF would want progress/yield, but a pilot PDF is fine.
The live Gate (a seeded annotated PDF: scan, review, import) is a browser pass.
Rungs 2 and 3 (flattened scans) still need a raster source; they are not mounted here.
